newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian ex-police face jail term over beating.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian ex-police face jail term over beating.

text.p: Four Indonesian policemen were facing jail terms of 24 to 32 months for the beating of an Islamic religious teacher that sparked a riot in West Java, the official Antara news agency reported on Wednesday.

It quoted prosecutor Colonel Ismail Bangun as telling a military tribunal on Tuesday that the defendants, a corporal and three sergeants, beat teacher Mahmud Farid and two of his students during interrogations in Tasikmalaya in late December.
The four men have already been discharged from the police.

Bangun said the beatings occurred after the son of the main defendant, identified only as corporal Nur, had been punished for stealing money from other students at a Moslem boarding school where Farid taught.
Reports of the beating spread in Tasikmalaya and a mob of mainly Moslems later burned shops, police stations and churches. Four people died in the disturbance.
Authorities have said 22 civilians will soon be tried for taking part in the riot. One of the accused had been charged with subversion, which carries a possible death penalty.
